title: Smart trace resampler for high-cardinality services with Tempo bulk-translation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a smart resampling pipeline in the OTLP/collector layer that detects sources with extremely high tag/span cardinality, applies canonicalization and operation-level mappings, and performs adaptive probabilistic sampling while preserving rare/error spans. The output will be bulk-translated to a Tempo-friendly schema and exported with a compact envelope to limit ingestion cost and index cardinality. Goals: reduce unique tag cardinality by ~90% for noisy services, lower Tempo ingest volume by ~60% for identified traffic, and keep per-request pipeline overhead <50ms p50. This work includes: design doc, prototype in collector filters, integration tests, load benchmarks, rollout plan, and dashboards to monitor sampling fidelity and error telemetry.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Asha Patel created ticket. Initial problem statement: several services (analytics-worker, ad-renderer) produced extreme cardinality (>1M unique span tags/day) causing Tempo ingestion cost spikes and query slowness. Proposal: combine canonicalization + adaptive resampling before export.

2025-02-20 - Design review with Observability and Runtime teams. Decision: implement as an OTLP pipeline stage (collector/relay) so both hosted and private deployments can adopt. Approved mapping ruleset format as a lightweight JSON manifest stored in S3/ConfigService.

2025-02-27 - Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/collector/PR-438 (collector/filter/resampler). Prototype implements a two-stage flow: 1) tag normalization using mapping rules, 2) reservoir sampler with per-operation error preservation. Performance microbenchmarks: additional CPU ~8% at 100k rps; p50 latency added ~12ms. Posting link to artifact: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/resampler-proto-v1.md

2025-03-03 - Feedback from Runtime (Marcus Nguyen): tighten SLOs for latency and memory. Action: add fast-path for small spans, limit state kept per-tenant to 10k keys, and use LRU eviction for mapping cache. Marcus assigned to implement cache eviction and metrics emission (resampler.accepted, resampler.dropped, resampler.error_preserved).

2025-03-04 - QA results: end-to-end run with fuzzed high-cardinality data. Observed ~87% reduction in unique tag combinations for analytics-worker and 62% lower exported span volume to Tempo ingest pipeline. Two regression issues found: a corner-case where linked spans for long traces were sampled inconsistently (reported as sub-issue ENG-517891). Plan: fix trace-consistent sampling using trace-id sticky reservoir and add unit tests.

Implementation notes: use map-file for canonicalization with versioning; expose per-tenant override to disable resampling; emit sanity counters and sampling-ratio histograms to internal metrics; implement rollout via feature-flag and canary rule targeting one org (acme-corp) first.

Related artifacts: design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Smart+Trace+Resampler, benchmark dashboard https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/resampler-bench (internal), PR link: github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/438, rollout runbook in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/runbooks/resampler-rollout.md
